title: Case study: FMEA risk on a pilot submission
text: Mitigation point exercise. Suppose team addresses two highest-RPN risks: add missing SDTM variables document ADaM derivation, lowers probability detectability difficulty. apply_mitigations() takes updates recomputes RPNs levels.
code: ranked <- rr[order(-rr$rpn), c("risk_id", "description", "rpn", "risk_level")] head(ranked, 3) #> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `status`. #> ℹ Risk Register: 3 risk(s), 0 open #> ℹ   Critical: 0, High: 3, Mean RPN: 48 #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   risk_id  description                                           rpn risk_level #>   <chr>    <chr>                                               <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 RISK-006 Laboratory units not standardized across sites         48 high       #> 2 RISK-008 Traceability gap: ADLB.BASE derivation undocumented    48 high       #> 3 RISK-013 Incomplete audit trail for manual data corrections     48 high top_two <- head(ranked$risk_id, 2)  updates <- data.frame(   risk_id       = top_two,   probability   = c(1, 2),   detectability = c(1, 1),   status        = "mitigated",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  rr_after <- apply_mitigations(rr, updates)

title: Risk Management with r4subrisk
text: FMEA (probability times impact times detectability) default, scoring rule pluggable. risk_model_probability_impact() drops detectability two-factor matrix, risk_model_ich_q9() gives qualitative acceptable, tolerable, unacceptable ranking. model normalizes 0-100 score, Risk pillar consumes way. use rule, build risk_model() scoring function, maximum raw score normalization, level bands:
code: risks <- data.frame(   risk_id = c("R001", "R002"),   description = c("Missing vars", "Bad derivation"),   probability = c(4, 3), impact = c(5, 4), detectability = c(2, 3) )  apply_risk_model(risks, risk_model_probability_impact()) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level model              #>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <chr>              #> 1 R001           20         80 critical   probability_impact #> 2 R002           12         48 high       probability_impact apply_risk_model(risks, risk_model_ich_q9()) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level   model  #>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>        <chr>  #> 1 R001            9      100   unacceptable ich_q9 #> 2 R002            6       66.7 unacceptable ich_q9 impact_only <- risk_model(   name = "impact_only",   score = function(df) df$impact,   max_raw = 5,   bands = list(high = c(4, 5), medium = c(3, 3), low = c(1, 2)),   required = "impact" ) apply_risk_model(risks, impact_only) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level model       #>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <chr>       #> 1 R001            5        100 high       impact_only #> 2 R002            4         80 high       impact_only

title: r4subrisk: Risk Quantification for Clinical Submissions
code: library(r4subcore) library(r4subrisk)  # Build a risk register manually risks <- data.frame(   risk_id       = c("R001", "R002"),   description   = c("Missing SDTM variables", "Unmapped ADaM derivations"),   category      = c("data_quality", "traceability"),   probability   = c(4, 3),   impact        = c(5, 4),   detectability = c(2, 3) )  rr     <- create_risk_register(risks) scores <- compute_risk_scores(rr)  # Or derive risks from an evidence table risk_items <- evidence_to_risks(evidence) rr <- create_risk_register(risk_items)  # Emit r4subcore-compatible evidence rows ctx <- r4sub_run_context(study_id = "ABC123", environment = "DEV") ev  <- risk_register_to_evidence(rr, ctx = ctx)  # Share or re-import a register (CSV, or xlsx with writexl/readxl installed). # On import the RPN and risk levels are recomputed from the assessed scores. write_risk_register(rr, "risk_register.csv") rr <- read_risk_register("risk_register.csv")  # Track risk falling across submission milestones trend <- risk_trend(list(baseline = rr_m1, interim = rr_m2, final = rr_m3)) plot_risk_trend(trend)  # ggplot burndown when ggplot2 is available

title: r4subrisk (development version)
text: Add reconcile_risk_registers(), item-level audit changed two versions risk register (prior vs current draft, two assessors’ registers). aligns rows risk_id labels risk added, removed, changed, unchanged; changed risks reports fields differ (description, category, probability, impact, detectability, owner, mitigation, status) tidy field_changes audit, prior current values side side. RPN movement read register’s stored rpn (nothing recomputed invented); purely structural diff. complements risk_trend() (trajectory many milestones) line--line view single pair. Fix documented return value compare_risk_registers(): rpn_changes tibble risks common registers (unchanged ones included, zero delta), whose RPN changed. Add risk_pareto(), Pareto (“vital ”) prioritization register. ranks risks stored RPN (recomputing nothing), reports risk’s share running cumulative share total RPN, flags smallest top run risks together carry caller-supplied cumulative share (cum_cutoff, default 0.8, usual Pareto 80 percent). cutoff reporting convention cumulative RPN share, risk, severity, RPN threshold. plot_risk_pareto() draws classic bar-plus-cumulative-line Pareto chart ggplot2 available. Add write_risk_register() read_risk_register() risk register import/export round-trip. Registers export CSV (xlsx writexl / readxl installed) faithful, human-readable snapshot. import file rebuilt create_risk_register(), canonical schema, RPN, risk-level classification recomputed assessed scores rather trusted file; write -> read cycle reproduces equivalent register. Add risk_trend(), turns named, ordered list risk registers (one per submission milestone) tidy burndown tibble: per milestone total RPN, mean RPN, number risks, open-critical count. stored RPN risk levels reused -, scoring recomputed. plot_risk_trend() draws burndown ggplot line chart ggplot2 available. Import %||% rlang package works declared minimum R version (R >= 4.2); operator became part base R 4.4.0. Fix “Risk Management” vignette: mitigation example now uses probability, impact, detectability columns apply_mitigations() actually reads (previously *_residual columns silently ignored, /comparison showed change), configuration example longer references non-existent required_origins field.
